title: Study one wisdom tradition beyond its slogans

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Studying a tradition requires primary wording, historical situation, an exemplar and living interpretation. One phrase cannot settle all four. A contemporary community’s self-description is evidence of its own aims, not of every adherent or ancient author.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Interpretation exercise accompanying the assigned sources: learner A writes “distinguishing what I choose from what happens means other people’s suffering is irrelevant.” Learner B writes “I can choose my response while taking another person’s need seriously; whether help succeeds is not fully mine to decide.” Neither sentence is a quotation. Keep actual passages open for the source-based practice.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Compare A/B against the assigned texts, locate the relevant passage and note an interpretive limit. Draft one small appropriate action; if a source cannot be accessed, label that comparison unverified rather than inventing words.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A modern community page describes its own inclusive events. Can this establish that every historical practitioner used the same interpretation?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: A turns a distinction about agency into a blanket moral dismissal not established by the supplied sentence. B preserves agency and possible responsibility without promising outcomes. Cite what the actual passage does and does not support. Partial: prefer B without textual support. Incorrect: invent a quotation or treat ancient social assumptions as binding modern instructions. The live action and tradition membership remain separate.
criteria: Source access and actual practice are reported honestly

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. It establishes a self-described contemporary position. Compare dated primary/context sources for the historical claim; continuity and difference both need evidence.
criteria: Source access and actual practice are reported honestly
